nodes.label: Tendril Network Hub Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The hero art depicts a single central figure grasping many bundles of threads that radiate outward to the edges of the frame, over a backdrop of branching lightning/tendril textures. This visually encodes the Tendril product idea: a central coordinator holding many outbound connections (nodes/leases/tunnels), i.e. one hub managing many distributed endpoints. The classical engraving style rendered in electric blue suggests old-world craft fused with electric/technical infrastructure.

nodes.label: Caveman Response Style Convention
nodes.rationale: Terse agent prose keeps all technical substance while dropping articles, filler, hedging and pleasantries so responses cost fewer tokens; code, commits and PRs stay in normal prose, and the style is auto-dropped for security warnings, irreversible actions, or a confused user.

nodes.label: Tendril
nodes.rationale: A pay-per-call compute marketplace for individual contributors rather than data centers — an agent-first, individual-scale take on Akash/io.net where anyone rents out their PC's CPU/RAM/GPU and is paid on-chain in USDC.

nodes.label: x402 Payment Protocol
nodes.rationale: x402 is the only door to paid functionality: an unpaid request to a payable endpoint returns HTTP 402 naming an exact USDC amount, the client builds an Algorand atomic group (own asset transfer plus the facilitator's unsigned fee txn), signs only its own, and retries. Payment IS identity, so no sign-up or sign-in is needed.

nodes.label: Payable Endpoints
nodes.rationale: GET /explorer stays free so an agent can survey live nodes and choose for itself; everything that costs money (topup, flat /rent/:id, /lease/:id/run, metered /x402/rent/:id) is x402-gated. Payable routes are deliberately CORS-free so any browser or headless agent can pay one — the Tendril web app has no privileged access.

nodes.label: Flat-Price Rent
nodes.rationale: Flat rent (FLAT_RENT_ATOMIC, 0.01 USDC) is deliberately independent of the node's hourly rate — that independence is what makes it flat. No quote, no credit arithmetic, no session. The contributor is paid a cut of what was actually paid, not of the list price, so money in and money out stay equal.

nodes.label: Metered Rent Pricing
nodes.rationale: POST /x402/rent/:nodeId?seconds=<n> prices as ceil(seconds/3600 x rate) minus existing credit, so the 402 asks only for the remainder — with enough credit there is no 402 and zero wallet popups at all.

nodes.label: USDC Pricing Model
nodes.rationale: Nodes are priced in USD per hour (PRICE_PER_HOUR_USD). USDC is a dollar with 6 decimals, so PRICE_PER_HOUR_USD x 1e6 is the atomic rate — there is no exchange rate to set or keep current. Because the facilitator sponsors the network fee, a client needs USDC and zero ALGO.

nodes.label: Prepaid Block Billing
nodes.rationale: A lease is a prepaid block of seconds: the full quote is charged up front and the unused remainder is refunded as credit when the lease closes, prorated at elapsed/3600 x rate. That refund is what makes the next 402 for that address smaller.

nodes.label: Prepaid Credit Ledger
nodes.rationale: Custodial off-chain ledger in Neon: payments pool at one platform address, and credit is keyed to the sender of the settled transaction, never to anything the client claims about itself. Every payment is recorded by txid so replaying one cannot credit twice; a topup writes one topups row and raises the credits balance in a single transaction.

nodes.label: Neon Postgres (money state)
nodes.rationale: Only money state hits the DB (credits, topups, charges, payouts). Nodes, leases, heartbeats and the watchdog stay in memory so the database stays quiet.

nodes.label: Per-Network Postgres Schemas
nodes.rationale: One database, one schema per network (testnet.* / mainnet.*), with the connection's search_path pointed at the right one so every query resolves to that network's tables and testnet play money can never be read as a mainnet balance. Both schemas are created at boot; public deliberately holds no tables.

nodes.label: Testnet/Mainnet Network Switch
nodes.rationale: ALGORAND_NETWORK (and build-time VITE_ALGORAND_NETWORK) is one switch from which the CAIP-2 id, algod endpoint, USDC asset id (10458941 testnet / 31566704 mainnet) and explorer all derive, so the pieces cannot be left half-migrated. An unrecognised value throws at boot: silently running testnet while believing you configured mainnet is worse than not starting.

nodes.label: x402 Facilitator
nodes.rationale: The facilitator verifies the atomic group by simulation, sponsors the network fee (so clients need zero ALGO), and settles on-chain only after the backend has provisioned.

nodes.label: Verify → Provision → Settle Ordering
nodes.rationale: Settlement is deliberately last: verify, do the work, then settle. A sandbox that fails to start returns 503 with nothing settled, so a failed rent costs the caller nothing.

nodes.label: Bazaar Discovery
nodes.rationale: Settling payments and being discoverable are separate systems — a settlement proves only that an address paid an amount, carrying no method, input shape or example output to build a catalog entry from. Tendril declares that metadata in every 402 (PUBLIC_BASE_URL, X402_TAG, X402_SERVICE_NAME, X402_ICON_URL); discovery canonicalises on PUBLIC_BASE_URL, so leaving it unset behind a proxy catalogs an unreachable localhost. Discovery is triggered by a settled payment, so a rent covered entirely by credit needs ?credit=none to be cataloged.

nodes.label: backend/src/x402/discovery.ts (route declarations)
nodes.rationale: Every payable route is declared in one place; adding an endpoint means adding an entry there and passing it to requirePayment. An endpoint that skips it still takes payments, it just stays invisible to discovery.

nodes.label: Trust Model (ephemeral container boundary)
nodes.rationale: A contributor gives compute, never filesystem or account access. The safety boundary is an ephemeral Docker container rather than a permissions system: no host mounts (-v never used), no inbound host ports, --cap-drop ALL plus only what sshd needs, --security-opt no-new-privileges, hard CPU/memory/PID cgroup caps, and destruction the moment the paid lease ends. Same containerization trade-off the DePIN compute sector already runs on, just prepaid and individual-scale.

nodes.label: SSH Sandbox Container
nodes.rationale: A hardened throwaway root container per lease. SSH auth is either an sshPubKey supplied in the rent body (authMethod publickey — the only option that works without a session, since there is no wallet address to use as a password) or a per-lease password equal to the wallet address, acceptable only because the compute is ephemeral.

nodes.label: bore Tunnel
nodes.rationale: The sandbox dials OUT over a bore tunnel so the contributor needs no inbound ports; TUNNEL_MODE=local publishes SSH to 127.0.0.1 when consumer and agent share a machine. bore is compiled from source on the first rent (~30s) because no arm64-linux binary ships, then cached.

nodes.label: On-Chain Contributor Payout
nodes.rationale: When a lease ends the contributor is paid on-chain in USDC minus PLATFORM_FEE_PCT, signed with PLATFORM_PRIVATE_KEY. If that key is unset or the payout address never opted into the asset, the payout is recorded as unpaid (txid null) and the node is flagged payoutBlocked rather than silently lost.

nodes.label: Lease Watchdog
nodes.rationale: Ends a lease when its prepaid time runs out, polling only every METER_INTERVAL_MS so worst-case overrun is one tick — a deliberate trade to keep heartbeats and metering out of Postgres.

nodes.label: In-Memory Node & Lease Registry
nodes.rationale: Nodes and leases live in memory, so a registry restart drops live sessions (the sockets die anyway). This is what keeps the DB quiet — heartbeats and the watchdog never write to Postgres.

nodes.label: Payment-as-Identity Auth
nodes.rationale: Paying needs no account at all — the settled transaction's sender is the identity. A session token (minted after signing a login nonce) is only needed to spend existing credit. Unauthenticated callers may hint ?payer= but the discount is floored at MIN_PAYABLE_ATOMIC so nobody can drain a stranger's balance.

nodes.label: backend/ (Registry + API)
nodes.rationale: Express + Neon Postgres + socket.io. Hosts the free /explorer, flat and metered payable routes, the watchdog, and on-chain payout. Only money state hits the DB.

nodes.label: contributor/ (Contributor Daemon)
nodes.rationale: Proves node ownership by signing a nonce, heartbeats over WebSocket, and on a lease launches the hardened SSH sandbox as a sibling container on the host Docker daemon (mounts the host socket rather than running Docker-in-Docker, so there is nothing extra to install).

nodes.label: web/ (Vite React SPA)
nodes.rationale: Vite + React + @txnlab/use-wallet (Pera/Defly), deliberately not Next.js: the wallet stack is client-only, so an SPA avoids SSR/hydration friction. It is just another x402 client with no privileged access.

nodes.label: example-buyer/ (Autonomous Agent)
nodes.rationale: Headless training agent proving the no-sign-in path: tops up over x402, discovers, rents, runs a script, releases — zero clicks, the payment is the identity.

nodes.label: shared/ (@tendril/shared)
nodes.rationale: Shared types, the WebSocket contract, and pricing helpers imported by every other workspace so the pricing math and socket protocol cannot drift between pieces.
